messages:
jess_sales: Hey team — Greenline legal asked for a signed pen-test confirmation letter and ISO artifacts for the POC. They want it by EOD tomorrow. Prospect contact is emily@greenline.com. Any standard route?

alex.k: We do have a standard pen-test authorization/attestation we can sign. It’s an internal letter signed by VP Security. I can generate it, but need the customer legal name + address and the scope they want us to assert (e.g., hosted API only vs. on-prem). Do we know scope for Greenline?

jess_sales: Scope is hosted API (no dedicated/private yet), just the POI for their legal team: "SOC 2 status, pen-test attestation, and ISO artifact list". They also asked if we can provide a redacted SOC 2 report — we usually provide an SOC 2 letter of attestation + certificate, right?

alex.k: Correct. We provide: 
- SOC 2 Type II attestation letter (redacted report on request)
- Pen-test attestation letter (signed)
- ISO 27001: we can share our certificate if we have one; if not, we provide the list of ISO artifacts (SoA, risk assessment summary, relevant policies).

morgan_pm: FYI for the POC budget: if legal requires a signed pen-test result rather than an attestation letter, that usually triggers a deeper review and we may need support from GTM to approve. For now ask for the minimal doc they accept.

ravi_eng: Tagging what Alex said — also include this snippet they can paste into their legal template if needed: 
```
Redwood Inference confirms that as of the date of this letter: 
1) Redwood has completed third-party penetration testing of the hosted inference infrastructure within the last 12 months.
2) Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II controls for the in-scope services.
3) Upon request, Redwood can provide a redacted SOC 2 report and a signed pen-test attestation letter.
```

alex.k: Action items: 
1) jess_sales — confirm exact legal entity name and address for the signing block and the email for delivery.
2) morgan_pm — confirm whether a redacted SOC 2 report is acceptable or if they specifically want a certified copy.
3) alex.k — I’ll prepare the pen-test letter template and share a PDF for signature.

jess_sales: Entity: Greenline Technologies, Inc., 240 Market St, Suite 900, SF CA 94105. Delivery email: emily@greenline.com. I’ll ask if redacted SOC2 is acceptable.

security_bot: Automated reminder: pen-test attestation template v2 located at https://internal.redwood/docs/sec/pen-test-letter-v2.pdf (access controlled).

alex.k: I pulled the template and populated the signing block. Sending the draft now to security@redwood.com for VP signature. Expect a signed PDF within 6 business hours once security confirms.

morgan_pm: One more note — Greenline asked about whether any customer data would be shared with the pen-test vendor. Tell them we never share customer data as part of routine vendor tests; scope is infrastructure and service config only. If they require scenario-based tests using sample data, legal needs to sign an additional agreement.

jess_sales: Noted. I told Emily: we can provide the attestation and redacted SOC2; if they insist on raw pen-test reports or testings involving their data we need extra approvals. She replied :thumbsup: and asked for the ETA.

alex.k: ETA — I’ll post the signed letter here once I get it. If legal wants the redacted SOC2, loop in compliance@redwood.com; they handle redaction and packaging.

jess_sales: Thanks. I’ll ask Greenline if redacted SOC2 is fine or if they require more. Will update here.

morgan_pm: Also adding that POC pricing credits and any extended SLA requests should be handled as a separate thread — don't mix with legal docs.

jess_sales: Understood — will keep docs thread separate. Closing loop once I have confirmation from Emily.
